chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The guarantee of the pilgrim (for Hajj) and the pilgrim (for Umrah) is upon Allah: if He keeps him alive, He brings him back to his family; and if He causes him to die, He enters him into Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the divine guarantee for a pilgrim who dies during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the comprehensive divine guarantee (daman) for pilgrims, emphasizing that Allah assumes full responsibility for their outcome. This dual promise—safe return to family or entry into Paradise—underscores the spiritual security and high status of Hajj and Umrah in Shia tradition, encouraging believers to undertake these rites with confidence in Allah's mercy.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The guarantee of the Pilgrim of Hajj and the Pilgrim of Umra is upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Keep him alive and Make him reach back to his family. And if he was to die, Enter him into the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Allah has undertaken the responsibility toward those who perform Hajj or ‘Umrah to join them with their families if He decides to keep them living, or admit them in paradise if He decides to cause them to die.’”
